candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata (Register of Payment Institutions and their Agents)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative statutory enumeration of every licensed payment institution in Montenegro, plus branches, agents, registered account-information-service providers, and a separate list of providers whose activities are NOT deemed payment services. Observed content enumerated seven licensees (Montenegro Transfers, Capital Transfer MNE, Moneta MNE, PaySpot ME, Alta Pay Group, PrestoPay, Business integration and business intelligence d.o.o.), each with its own PDF entry. This is the master snowball node for the whole non-bank payments cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML scrape of the register page plus download of each per-institution PDF; diff entity list quarterly to detect new licences, agent additions and withdrawals.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language regulator-register search, then direct fetch

Montenegro registered payment institutions e-money issuers register CBCG

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata (Register of E-money Institutions)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory register of e-money issuers, their branches and agents. As observed, the register currently states no e-money institution is entered — itself a first-order market fact (no domestic e-money licensee in Montenegro), and the page is the tripwire that will show the first entrant.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly HTML fetch with change detection on the 'no institutions registered' notice; alert on any first entry.
candidates.discovered_via_method: regulator register index page
queries_used: CBCG registar platnih institucija institucija elektronskog novca Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Podaci o platnim uslugama i elektronskom novcu (Payment services and e-money statistics)
candidates.why_relevant: Highest-value quantitative source for this cell: quarterly statistics reported by payment service providers AND e-money issuers under the Odluka o izvještajima o platnom prometu. Observed tables cover users by payment-service type, issued payment cards, card-acceptance devices (POS/ATM terminals), transactions by service type, domestic and cross-border card/e-money transactions, transactions by terminal type, contactless transactions, and cash deposits/withdrawals — i.e. exactly the ATM/POS, card and cash-usage series in scope. Distributed as downloadable ZIP archives; latest observed Q1 2026.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly scheduled crawl of the release page, download each ZIP, unpack and parse the tabular workbooks into a time series keyed on quarter and indicator.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language statistics search, then direct fetch
queries_used: CBCG statistika platnog prometa platne institucije izvještaj

Gives the settlement-layer denominator against which non-bank payment-institution flows can be sized, and now also covers SEPA and the domestic instant-payments (TIPS clone) rails.

candidates.why_relevant: The statute that defines what a payment institution and an e-money institution are, which activities require a licence, and which reporting obligations generate the public statistics. negative_findings.description: The CBCG Register of E-money Institutions was fetched directly and states, in Montenegrin, that no e-money institution is currently entered ('U Registru trenutno nema upisane institucije za elektronski novac').
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero licensed domestic e-money issuers in Montenegro at time of scouting. Any Montenegrin 'e-wallet' proposition therefore operates under a payment-institution licence, a bank, or a foreign passport — not a domestic e-money licence.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Removes an entire expected source family from the cell. Analysts must not infer e-money volumes from a register that has no members, and the CBCG e-money statistics tables will be structurally sparse for domestic issuers.

negative_findings.description: Two entities in the CBCG payment-institution register — 'Business integration and business intelligence d.o.o. Podgorica' and 'Capital Transfer MNE d.o.o. Podgorica' — could not be matched to a confirmed corporate website in either Montenegrin or English search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Capital Transfer MNE appears only as a name in aggregator and secondary text; the BIBI entity produced no usable web presence at all. Their register PDFs on cbcg.me remain the only located primary evidence.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Two of seven licensees are effectively invisible outside the register, so licensee counts overstate the number of observable, quantifiable actors. Their volumes must be reached via CRPS financial statements rather than own publications.

negative_findings.description: No source was found in which Montenegrin payment institutions publish their own transaction volumes or values. Searches in Montenegrin for licensee names combined with volume terms returned marketing pages, hiring notices and press interviews only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Licensee 'own published volumes' — a premise of this cell's brief — largely do not exist as public disclosures in Montenegro. Coverage, tariffs, service catalogues and location counts are published; transaction counts are not.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Non-bank payment flow sizing must be built from the CBCG aggregate quarterly payment-services statistics and from CRPS-filed financial statements, not from licensee self-reporting. Setting this expectation early prevents a fruitless collection stream.

negative_findings.description: Secondary sources disagree on the ownership of Montenegro Transfers d.o.o. Podgorica: one attributes it to the Alta group (alongside Alta Pay Podgorica), another states Eki Transfers holds 100%.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ownership unresolved from open web sources; both claims are secondary and neither was corroborated against a primary filing in this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Group structure determines whether Montenegro's two largest remittance agents are independent competitors or one economic actor — a material distinction for concentration analysis. Must be settled against CRPS before publication.

negative_findings.description: No established Montenegrin-language term or public register was located for crypto-asset service providers / VASPs operating as payment-adjacent actors; searches around fintech licensing surfaced only payment-institution and e-money categories.
negative_findings.result_summary: No MiCA-equivalent Montenegrin register or licensee list found in this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If crypto on/off-ramps are in scope for the payments landscape, this cell currently has no local-language vocabulary or pointer source for them, and the gap is unmeasured rather than empty.

negative_findings.description: The CBCG sub-page specifically holding 'Finansijski izvještaji platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac' was referenced in search snippets but its exact URL was not confirmed by direct fetch; the supervision-section landing page was recorded instead with reduced confidence.
negative_findings.result_summary: Firm-level financial reports for payment institutions are believed published by CBCG, exact location unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is potentially the single best firm-level quantitative source in the cell. It should be located by crawling the supervision section tree before concluding it does not exist.

coverage_gaps.description: The CBCG page hosting financial reports of payment institutions and e-money institutions was not pinned to a confirmed URL.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Crawl https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/kontrolna-funkcija/ and the platni promet tree exhaustively (both /me/ and /en/ locales) to locate the payment-institution financial-reports page, then register it as a first-class direct source.

coverage_gaps.description: Telco-operated payment and mobile-money propositions were not systematically scouted. MTEL was observed acting as a Western Union agent, and Crnogorski Telekom and One Montenegro recur in adjacent search results, but none was investigated as a payment actor.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated Montenegrin-language sweep on 'mobilno plaćanje', 'm-novčanik', 'plaćanje računa putem mobilnog operatora', 'MTEL uplata', 'One Montenegro plaćanje' and check whether any telco appears in the CBCG register or acts only as an agent of a licensee.

coverage_gaps.description: Card acquiring and payment-gateway/PSP layer (e-commerce acquirers, card processors serving Montenegrin merchants) was not covered — this cell reached POS/ATM data only through the CBCG aggregate statistics, not through the processors themselves.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout in Montenegrin for 'procesiranje kartica', 'ekvajering', 'platni gateway Crna Gora', 'online plaćanje karticom prodavac' and identify whether processing is done in-house by banks or by regional processors; check whether any appears as a 'provider of services not deemed payment services' in the CBCG register annex.

coverage_gaps.description: The CBCG register's annexed list 'Pružaoci usluga koji obavljaju aktivnosti koje se ne smatraju platnim uslugama' (providers of services not deemed payment services) was observed to exist but was not opened or enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Download and parse that PDF — it is a second, less-known actor list that likely names technical service providers, gateways and closed-loop schemes invisible in the main register.

coverage_gaps.description: Searches were run in Montenegrin/Serbian (Latin) and English only. Cyrillic-script variants and Albanian-language sources serving the Ulcinj/Plav populations — relevant for remittance corridors — were not queried.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Repeat core queries in Cyrillic ('регистар платних институција', 'електронски новац') and in Albanian ('institucionet e pagesave Mali i Zi', 'transferta parash') to catch agent networks and diaspora remittance actors missed by Latin-script search.

coverage_gaps.description: No historical archive strategy was established for the registers, which are overwritten in place rather than versioned.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snapshot all four CBCG registers into a versioned store from first collection onward, and back-fill earlier states from the Internet Archive, so licensee entry and exit can be dated rather than merely observed.

coverage_gaps.description: EU/EEA-passported payment institutions and e-money issuers serving Montenegrin residents were not scouted. Montenegro is not an EU member but joined SEPA in 2025, so foreign-licensed providers may serve the market without appearing in any CBCG register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check whether CBCG publishes any notification list for foreign providers operating cross-border into Montenegro, and cross-reference EBA registers for firms declaring Montenegro coverage post-SEPA accession.

brief: Montenegro's non-bank payments landscape is small, fully enumerable, and anchored on one authoritative pointer: the CBCG Register of Payment Institutions, which lists seven licensees (Montenegro Transfers, Capital Transfer MNE, Moneta MNE, PaySpot ME, Alta Pay Group, PrestoPay, and Business integration and business intelligence d.o.o.), while the parallel Register of E-money Institutions is explicitly empty — there is currently no domestic e-money licensee. Quantitatively, the cell rests on CBCG's quarterly 'Podaci o platnim uslugama i elektronskom novcu' release, which covers cards issued, acceptance devices, transactions by service and terminal type, contactless, cross-border card use and cash deposits/withdrawals in downloadable archives, supplemented by the RTGS/DNS payment-system statistics and the newly live SEPA and instant-payment rails. The licensees themselves publish service catalogues, tariffs, agent-network coverage and open-banking bank-connection lists (PrestoPay's multibanking pages are unusually revealing) but no transaction volumes, so firm-level sizing must come from CRPS-filed financial statements and, if located, CBCG's payment-institution financial reports. The main open risks are two register entities with no discoverable web presence, an unscouted card-acquiring and gateway layer, and unresolved group ownership across the two dominant remittance agents.
